elements.element: Customer has an operative right to terminate the Vendor for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1A permits the Issuer to terminate only “at the direction of the Depositor.” Thus, the Issuer does not have an independent Customer termination right; exercise depends on another party's direction.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1A expressly provides for termination “at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice.”

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: The Servicer must “refund any Servicing Fee paid in respect of the period after the effective date,” which operationally provides the required pro-rata refund of prepaid post-termination fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1 prohibits the Servicer from resigning unless it determines that it is legally unable to perform. Legal inability is not convenience, and no other Vendor convenience-termination right is provided.

elements.element: Customer has an operative right to terminate the Vendor for convenience.
elements.evidence: The Issuer's right is conditioned on direction from the Depositor, so the operative language does not give the Customer an independent termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1A requires only thirty (30) days' prior written notice, outside the fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1A expressly permits termination without any termination fee, penalty, make-whole, or other compensation. A zero fee is below the permitted cap.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination-for-convenience right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right exists: Section 7.1 permits resignation only for legal inability. The conditional restriction is therefore satisfied because the relevant Vendor right is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right exists, so there is no circumstance in which Vendor may exercise such a right without the specified notice. Resignation for legal inability is not termination for convenience.

result.reason: Neither level is fully satisfied. The central defect is party direction: the Issuer may terminate only at the Depositor's direction, rather than having an independent Customer right. The fallback also fails because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90 days. The refund, absence of an early-termination fee, and prohibition on Vendor convenience termination are otherwise protective. The redline is not minimal because it adds partial-termination authority, additional notice recipients, fee-waiver language, successor-servicer mechanics, and resignation-related language beyond what was necessary. It generally preserves the existing servicing and transaction-document structure, but “in whole or in part” may interact awkwardly with successor-servicer provisions designed for a complete removal.
